QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_10

question.text: For Category I and II AIFs, benchmarking agencies typically construct 'vintage-year' benchmarks. What is a 'vintage year' in this context?

answer.text: The calendar year in which the fund files its final winding-up return with SEBI.
The year in which the benchmarking agency's data vendor was incorporated.
The year in which the fund achieves its First Close — used to group funds with comparable investment-deployment timelines.
The year in which the LP first recovers 100% of paid-in capital (DPI = 1.0).

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 7 footnote 60 and Section 7.6, vintage year refers to the milestone year in which the first influx of investment capital is deployed — in AIF context, typically anchored to First Close. Vintage grouping ensures apples-to-apples comparison because funds of the same vintage face the same macro entry pricing and exit conditions. The Trap: A is the wind-up, not vintage. B is unrelated. D is the 'DPI breakeven year', a separate performance milestone. Note: Vintage-year benchmarking is the core method for comparing Category I/II AIFs with similar first-close timelines.
